newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends a bit lower, eyeing dollar/yen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends a bit lower, eyeing dollar/yen.

text.p: The U.S. dollar's strength overseas pulled the Taiwan dollar to end slightly lower on Friday and dealers said it was likely to move around current levels unless the U.S. unit surges past 120 yen.
The rate moved in a T$27.421-505 range before ending at T$27.462, compared with Thursday's T$27.444 finish. Turnover slid to US$397.5 million from US$429 million.

The exchange rate has been moving sharply in recent sessions due to strong expectations for a traditional increase in Taiwan dollar liquidity demand before the Chinese lunar new year on February 7, dealers said.
The Taiwan unit's recent push to higher levels due to local factors was offset by the dramatic firmness of the greenback against major currencies in Asian trading, they added.

"The Taiwan dollar should continue moving sharply in active trade because of domestic expectations as well as overseas trends," said one dealer at a foreign bank, seeing a T$27.40-50 range in the near term.
"But if the U.S. dollar surges above 120 Japanese yen, the Taiwan dollar may test as low as T$27.55," the dealer added.
